structure: Part 8, Commodity search. Read search.fit.spec.js (describe 'commodity search', 14 tests, lines 63 to 228) and mined all 14 trace zips it produced, one per test, in read order (working folders s01..s14 under trace-animals-fit.work/part8/ map to lines 63, 76, 95, 103, 116, 126, 138, 153, 159, 176, 181, 193, 216, 228). The playwright trace CLI that tim runs refused these traces (TraceVersionError: created by a newer Playwright), so each zip's extracted trace, network and frame-snapshot records were read directly with jq: every action (before events), every localhost request with its form body, status and redirect, and the full DOM snapshot of each distinct page state rendered from main. Every test shares one set-up: stub sign-in, Start a new notification, origin answered (France, No) and saved, then the overview link 'What are you importing?' opens the page. One page is in scope: 'What are you importing?' at /live-animals/notifications/{ref}/commodities (caption 'About the consignment'), always reached from the overview. Its states, all on that one URL: empty (s01, s02 help opened); short query, no results (s03); results grouped by commodity (s04, s05, s06, s07, s14); no match (s08); a running selection panel with Clear all (s09, s12, s13, s14); validation error on empty submit (s11). Save and continue leads to Commodity details (/consignment-details, s12, s13), seen only for its species headings; the back link returns to the overview (s10). The axe test (s14) passed with help open, one species chosen and two result groups showing. Claims record the page skeleton, every field, result and panel copy, the selection and save behaviour, the form posts that carry them, the validation, and gaps for controls no test drove.

claims.statement: The commodity search page is reached from the notification overview through the link 'What are you importing?', and opens at /live-animals/notifications/{reference}/commodities.
claims.ref: trace s01 (search.fit.spec.js:63) action call@1577; GET /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-4JA500/commodities 200

claims.statement: On a new notification, the first Save and continue on the origin page redirects straight to the commodity search page rather than to the overview; a later origin save returns to the overview.
claims.ref: trace s01 network: POST /origin 302 -> /commodities; second POST /origin 302 -> /live-animals/notifications/GBN-AG-26-4JA500
claims.note: Seen in every trace's set-up; the origin page itself is another part's.

claims.quote: A commodity code describes a specific product when importing or exporting goods.

claims.statement: Searching 'Bos' returns one group, Cow (0102), with two species: Cattle (Bos spp.) and Domestic cattle (Bos taurus), in that order; American bison (Bison bison), also a Cow (0102) species, is not matched.

claims.statement: Each species is offered as its common name with its scientific name in brackets after it.

claims.statement: Two commodities may share a commodity code and still render as separate groups, keyed by commodity name (Cat and Dog both show 01061900).
claims.ref: trace s07 snapshot call@2027

claims.statement: The search matches by scientific name: 'Salmo' returns Fish (0301) with Atlantic salmon (Salmo salar); 'Bos taurus', 'Felis catus' and 'Bison bison' each return their species.
claims.ref: trace s09 snapshot call@1939 (Salmo); s12 actions call@1975 to call@1991

claims.statement: Each species checkbox is named species and carries the value '<commodity name>|<species id>' (for example Cow|1148346 for Domestic cattle, Cow|1388624 for Cattle (Bos spp.), Cow|716661 for American bison, Cat|923501, Dog|923502, Fish|801204).
claims.ref: trace s04 snapshot call@2021; s07 snapshot call@2027; s09 snapshot call@1939; s12 snapshot call@2001

claims.statement: The commodity and species list the search reads (commodity name, code, species common and scientific name, species id) is reference data looked up on the server; no browser call reveals which service holds it.
claims.ref: trace s04 network: only POST /commodities 200 seen from the browser
claims.note: The fit run used stubbed backends; the server-side reference-data call is not in a browser trace.

claims.statement: When a search of three or more characters matches nothing, the page says 'No results found' and lists no checkboxes.

claims.statement: The selection panel still shows species chosen under earlier queries while the current results show something else (Salmo results with Cow and Cat chosen).
claims.ref: trace s09 actions call@1939, call@1941, call@1943

claims.statement: The page has a primary 'Save and continue' button.
